newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-POIDEVIN CRITICISES SMITH'S TACTICS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-POIDEVIN CRITICISES SMITH'S TACTICS.

text.p: Former Australia test forward Simon Poidevin said the Wallabies are playing no better than a club side after labelling coach Greg Smith's tactics as outdated and confused.
"It's very frustrating watching the team playing like a club side," said Poidevin in reaction to New Zealand's crushing 33-18 win in a Tri-Nations test on Saturday.
"The Australian team's on-field performance seems confused and at times directionless," flanker Poidevin, Australia's most capped forward with 59 tests, told The Australian newspaper on Tuesday.

"Ultimately the responsibility for the style and tactics must lie with coach Greg Smith and assistants John Griffiths and Lloyd Walker," said Poidevin, who pointed to inconsistency in team selection as a major cause of Australia's current woes.
"The problem has been the number of (team) changes already. It seems the team has a revolving door and that has to stop -- but the right team has to be picked."
Smith, whose two-year contract expires at the end of 1997, will face growing pressure to keep his job if Australia lose to South Africa in a Tri-Nations clash in Brisbane on Saturday.
The Wallabies have lost twice to the All Blacks over the past month to present their trans-Tasman rivals the annual Bledisloe Cup.

In a separate development, the local media were scathing over the recall of fly-half David Knox to face the Springboks given Smith's repeated statements over the past month ruling out the veteran goal-kicker as a potential test candidate.
"If Smith was a gymnast, his backflip was worthy of an Olympic gold," The Australian commented, adding: "Smith must have been driven by panic or confusion in recalling Knox".
Only three days ago, Smith, one of Australia's three test selectors, described Knox as a "non-tackler" who posed too great a risk because of his defensive weaknesses.
But by Monday, when he announced a 23-man squad which included the ACT Brumbies goalkicker, Smith had changed his mind, describing Knox as an "automatic choice".
The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported that Smith's remarkable change of heart followed the intervention of Australian Rugby Union chief John O'Neill.
Knox, who is currently playing for Natal in South Africa's domestic Currie Cup competition, was summoned after Tim Horan broke his hand against New Zealand on Saturday.
Australia and South Africa both lost to New Zealand in their opening Tri-Nations matches.
